chapter: Later tours, illness and the union job
title: Bechet and the microphone; Teddy Buckner's high F
summary: Bechet stayed in front of the microphone, overrode the trumpet, and got furious when Teddy Buckner hit a high F.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: Yes, he didn't do anything else.
Well I heard the record but how did the whole thing come off? I mean was it enjoyable?

Yes. I enjoyed it. I really enjoyed it. Especially Vic and myself. We hadn't been to Belgium before and seeing all of these buildings, this big Russian building where we'd gone in. They served you free vodka. So Vic stayed in there all day. And different shows from the East. And it was just great.
Well what I really meant was you know, how was playing with Bechet I mean?

It was okay. It could have been better. I tell you one thing, I always had played, he played right in front of the mike. And I'm supposed to be playing the lead. I don't know how to play anything else, so he, sometimes he and I both would be playing the same lead.
Well he always had this tendency to override the trumpet. But it really didn't make too much sense.

No, and he stayed right in front of that mike even if I was playing a solo, I'd move, be way over to the side. So sometimes you can't hardly hear everything unless it was my specialty then I'd get it. But on those other songs he wouldn't move away from that mic and I just had to play over there, way over.

But he didn't do it deliberately, he had a, I guess that's just the way he thought it would be. But to me, we never knew when there was going, we taped every show every day. This is one that George picked out to make a record of.

Well, you know the very first, now when you made those records with your friend Tommy Ludnier you know in about 1933, it was the same thing, he was just sort of overriding the whole thing, it was the trombone......

I remember one time Teddy Beckner and Sidney Bechet was playing somewhere and Teddy, when they got to the end of the number, Teddy made a high F. Dammit that made him so mad he just, it just seemed that Teddy was trying to top him. He got so mad at Teddy he called the whole

band out on the stand and made them play the whole number again. Teddy made the high F again. (LAUGHTER). they almost had to separate them because he couldn't call them back to play it three times. Teddy did it purposely. But there is nothing wrong in him making a high note. But Sidney didn't want him to hit a note, anywhere near as high as he was hitting see.
That's strange, you know, with all the talent he had that he had to be like that.
